Hi Mina / Marissa,

Thanks for the call earlier. We pulled together a prioritized set of redlines against the renewal packet you sent (MSA + consolidated order form + Exhibit C). The attached doc has line-by-line comments — the areas we care about most are:

- Term alignment from 12 to 24 months (we prefer 24 but can be flexible if pricing adjusts)
- Capacity stacking vs. true-up cadence (want to avoid large mid-term bill shocks)
- Data residency language in Section 5 (legal needs stronger assurances; we operate in regulated healthcare workflows)
- SLA credits and measurement windows (we requested 30-day rolling windows)

We circled back to our procurement team and can sign quickly if we get: a) explicit commit to 24-month term at current tier pricing, or b) a detailed step for staged capacity uplift with prorated billing.

Subject: Re: Confluence renewal — redlines & capacity consolidation

Jordan — thanks for the clear prioritization. We reviewed the attached and pulled together internal proposed responses. High level:

1) Term: We can accommodate a 24-month term at current list price on the condition of a 10% prepayment, or alternately a 24-month commitment with the current incremental tier pricing. We put both options in Exhibit A (see attached Exhibit-C_capacity_schedule_v5.xlsx for staged uplift).

2) Capacity stacking / true-up: We propose a staging approach: monthly reporting + a capped quarterly true-up window (maximum quarterly true-up not to exceed 15% of committed capacity). This smooths billing while allowing you to ramp.

3) Data residency: Redwood will add the standard customer-controlled VPC commitment and a 3rd-party audit clause referencing our SOC2 + optional managed on-prem connector for regulated workloads. Legal suggested the specific language in Section 5.2 (redline in the doc).

4) SLA credits: Our standard measurement is a 30-day rolling average; we can add a 7-day lookback to help with transient blips. We pushed back on replacing rolling with calendar windows because that adds complexity operationally.

I've attached a consolidated redline (Confluence_OrderForm_Redline_v3.docx) and the updated capacity schedule. Marissa / Aditya — can you review the Exhibit-C numbers and confirm the billing proration formula? Jordan — we tried to capture your preference for staged uplift without mid-term shocks.

Thanks,
Mina
Sr. Account Executive — Strategic Renewals
Redwood Inference

Thanks Mina — quick notes from legal/billing side:

- Exhibit C numbers: Aditya and I adjusted the quarterly ramp so the committed capacity trajectory is: Q1 +0%, Q2 +25%, Q3 +45%, Q4 +60% (relative to current committed baseline). This is conservative but keeps quarterly true-ups below the 15% cap.
- Billing proration: Aditya confirmed we will prorate by day for mid-quarter activations and apply the quarterly cap before invoicing true-ups. Wording is in Section 2 of Exhibit C.
- Term/Payment: We can offer the 10% prepay discount (applied as an invoice credit at execution). Legal wants to avoid asymmetric termination cliffs — added a mutual termination right after 12 months for material breach with cure period.

Jordan / Priya — Marissa and I are comfortable moving this to contract negotiation on our side if you can confirm which term option you prefer (prepay vs. staged commitment). If you confirm prepay, we will add the credit line and hand to legal for sign-off.

-Marissa
